items.title: Sonny Henry Interview, 1959-01-08
items.q: He held my hand and showed me the second position... I'm going to give you this... come up here twice a week.

ctx.x: I think you might give your name first. Albert Warner. Any middle name? No, any middle name. Born

New Orleans, Louisiana. December 31st, 1890. I first started learning music with a half-brother mine. He learned from Honoré Dutré. Well, when he left, before he left, he bought him a new trombone. And a boy wanted to buy his old trombone from him. And he refused to sell it to him. He paid one against his brother. Well, he sent downtown, got me, and I went on up to his house to see what it was all about. I got there. He gave me this little old brass horn with about a bell the size of a saucer. A little chatois, a…
And, uh, had you played anything before that at all, like drums or guitar or anything?

items.title: Sonny Henry Interview, 1959-01-08
items.q: I heard this other boy, this boy. Lord Dutre.

ctx.x: Who were some of the trombonists when you first started playing that you heard?

I heard, uh, this fella, this young fella, yeah, he was, oh I can't think of that boy's name. He left, yeah, Zoo, Zoo Robertson. I was gonna ask you, just start asking, yeah, Zoo Robertson. Zoo Robertson? Well, he was a good friend of ours, you know. He was a good musician. Mm-hmm. Zoo Robertson, well, and I heard this other boy, this boy. Lord Dutre.
Dutre. He was a good one, too.
